name: @quickchatai/quickreview
//private: The root is the published `qcr` CLI: the whole app (TUI, daemon, companion, every verb), installed with npm, pnpm or bun. It depends on the pi plugin (packages/pi-plugin) at its exact version and on pi at the exact pins below. Publishing is a release step of its own, never part of a build.
description: QuickReview — a sovereign 24/7 AI code-review daemon: deterministic TypeScript core driving sticky LLM review sessions, with an operator TUI, Slack concierge, and a continuous learning loop your org owns end to end

repository.//: placeholder until the public repo exists (snapshot); update on first publish

//workspaces: The review core is its own package (packages/pi-plugin, the pi plugin). The app at the root declares it in dependencies at the exact workspace version, kept equal to this one's (tests/layers.test.ts), and npm links the workspace in its place.
//files: Exactly what the app reads at runtime from its package root: the build (dist/), the bin, the TypeScript sources pi loads as extensions (extensions/ and the src/ they import), the data the app and the companion read (agents/, prompts/, seeds/, schemas/, generic profiles/, skills/, the seed manifest), the scripts sessions and the bring-up run (scripts/), the deploy and docker files the onboarding, the companion and the memory sidecar use, and the shipped config defaults. Never tests, bench, docs, state, secrets, the private profile or the operator-only scripts; never a rulebook file. tests/cli-install-smoke.test.ts packs it and checks.

scripts.//canary:pi: The offline pi canaries (tests/pi-canary/): the real pi SDK at the pinned version on pi-ai's faux provider, so no network and no cost. They also run inside `npm test`; this is the named entry point CI requires whenever the pi dependencies change (a bump is gated by it).
scripts.//canary:pi:range: The same canaries on each pi version the plugin's peer range (packages/pi-plugin/package.json) should hold, refusing one outside it: no argument runs the installed pi; `-- --install 1.3.x` fetches another first (the registry: CI's pi-range matrix runs it in a fresh checkout). Needs the build.
scripts.//lint: Deliberately NOT chained into `test` or `build`: scripts/dev-tui.sh blocks on the build before the TUI paints (ruling 5), and an ESLint pass there is seconds of blank terminal. CI runs it as its own step.
scripts.//typecheck:tests: tests/ is excluded from the BUILD (it emits nothing), so nothing type-checked it and ~40 latent errors accumulated — three of them tests that were asserting nothing, plus three more that read the real filesystem while claiming to drive an injected seam. Deliberately NOT chained into `build`: `scripts/dev-tui.sh` blocks on that build before the TUI paints (ruling 5), and a second full tsc pass there is 7s of blank terminal. `tests/fences-gate.test.ts` runs this as part of the suite instead, which is this repo's CI.
scripts.//smoke:worker: The scripted worker smoke (replaces smoke:session): a worker is born, runs a round and is resumed on pi's SDK over pi-ai's faux provider. No tmux, no pi binary, no model, no network.

qcrPi.//: Named qcrPi, never `pi`: pi reads a package.json `pi` key as a package manifest, and this root is not a pi package (the plugin is packages/pi-plugin). pi and pi-ai are exact dependencies above (types for the extensions, and the VM boot's plain `npm ci` installs them beside the global CLI the image carries). This block is the mirror a bare checkout without config.toml reads: package and version must equal the dependencies, the lockfile, config.toml [pi], ansible group_vars and every Dockerfile ARG (tests/fences.test.ts [T12], tests/docker-daemon.test.ts). Lens sessions run through our own lens tools (src/engine/lens/), not a pi subagent extension, so no extra extension pin exists.
